symbols.name: X
symbols.space: a compact measurable space; \([0,1]\) on the primitive chart

symbols.name: P
symbols.type: law of one observed-data and potential-outcome draw

symbols.name: \gamma_a
symbols.def: the Hall exponent parameter when the propensity lower tail is polynomial, with the convention \(\gamma_a=\infty\) when \(\operatorname*{ess\,inf}\pi_a(X)>0\)

symbols.name: f_{a\mid X}
symbols.sig: \(f_{a\mid X}(y\mid x)\) is the conditional density of \(Y(a)\) given \(X=x\)

symbols.name: K_a
symbols.sig: \(t\mapsto K_a(t,\cdot)\) is a fixed Borel regular conditional law under \(P\) of \(Y(a)\) given \(\pi_a(X)=t\)

symbols.name: \kappa_{a,\tau}
symbols.sig: \(\kappa_{a,\tau}(t)=\int\psi_{a,\tau}(y)K_a(t,dy)\) is the score version induced by the chosen Borel regular conditional law

symbols.name: G_a
symbols.role: a representative endpoint outcome law whose pushforward through the finite score map determines the oracle limit

symbols.name: d_a
symbols.sig: \(d_a:[0,1]\to[0,1]\), with \(d_a(x)=0\) only at arm \(a\)'s weak-overlap endpoint

symbols.name: \vartheta_a
symbols.space: a prespecified element of a finite grid in \([0,\bar\vartheta]\)

symbols.name: \widehat p_{a,(j)}
symbols.def: the \(j\)-th order statistic of \(\{\widehat\pi_{a,-k(i)}(X_i):1\le i\le n\}\)

symbols.name: M_n
symbols.space: positive deterministic sequences diverging to infinity

symbols.name: E_{a,n}
symbols.def: \(E_{a,n}=\max_k\max_{i\in I_k:0<\pi_a(X_i)\le u_{a,n}}|\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(X_i)/\pi_a(X_i)-1|\), with an empty maximum equal to zero

symbols.name: \widehat q_a
symbols.sig: a sample map into \(\mathbb R^{|\mathcal T|}\)

symbols.name: \widetilde q_{a,-k}
symbols.sig: a training-fold map into \(\mathbb R^{|\mathcal T|}\)

symbols.name: k_n
symbols.space: positive integers with \(k_n\to\infty\), \(k_n/n\to0\), and \(k_n(k_n/n)^{1/(\gamma_a-1)}\to\infty\) uniformly over finite-index arms

symbols.name: \widehat\gamma_a
symbols.def: \(\widehat\gamma_a=1+\{k_n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k_n}\log(Z_{a,(j)}/Z_{a,(k_n+1)})\}^{-1}\), where the order statistics are decreasing and the value is \(+\infty\) when the denominator is zero

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_{a,\theta}
symbols.def: the fully empirical estimate in \(\text{def:drift-correction}\), set to zero on \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm G}\)

symbols.name: \widehat m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}
symbols.def: \(\widehat m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\widehat\pi_{a,-k(i)}(X_i)\le\widehat p_{a,(k_n)}\}\widetilde\psi_{a,\tau,-k(i)}(Y_i)}{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\widehat\pi_{a,-k(i)}(X_i)\le\widehat p_{a,(k_n)}\}}\), with value zero when the denominator is zero

symbols.name: \mathsf K_f
symbols.space: a fixed bounded nonnegative probability kernel

symbols.name: \omega_{a,n}
symbols.space: positive deterministic sequences with \(\omega_{a,n}\to0\), \(h_{a,n}/(n\omega_{a,n})\to0\) on \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\), and \((\sqrt n\,\omega_{a,n})^{-1}\to0\) on \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\)

symbols.name: \widehat f_a
symbols.def: \(\widehat f_a(\tau)=\max\{n^{-1/4},\frac{\sum_i\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}\mathsf K_f((Y_i-\widehat q_a(\tau))/\omega_{a,n})/[(\widehat\pi_{a,-k(i)}(X_i)\vee\widehat b_{a,n})\omega_{a,n}]}{\sum_i\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}/(\widehat\pi_{a,-k(i)}(X_i)\vee\widehat b_{a,n})}\}\), with the ratio set to zero when its denominator is zero

symbols.name: H_{a,n}
symbols.def: \(H_{a,n}=h_{a,n}\) on \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\) and \(H_{a,n}=\sqrt n\) on \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\)

symbols.name: \widehat H_{a,n}
symbols.def: \(\widehat H_{a,n}=\widehat h_{a,n}\) for \(a\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm H}\) and \(\widehat H_{a,n}=\sqrt n\) for \(a\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm G}\)

symbols.name: B
symbols.space: Conditionally on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), \(B\) is uniform over all \(b\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|b|=m\); each such set has conditional probability \(\binom{n}{m}^{-1}\).

symbols.name: \widehat q_{a,B}^{\mathrm{bc}}
symbols.def: the complete rule for \(\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}\) recomputed using only indices in \(B\)

symbols.name: \widehat H_{a,m,B}
symbols.def: the complete rule for \(\widehat H_{a,n}\) recomputed at sample size \(m\) using only indices in \(B\)

symbols.name: V_{B,a}
symbols.sig: \(V_{B,a}:\mathcal T\to\mathbb R\) is the armwise statistic constructed in \(\text{def:vector-subsampling}\)

symbols.name: T_{B,n}
symbols.sig: \(T_{B,n}:\mathcal T\to\mathbb R\) is the statistic constructed in \(\text{def:vector-subsampling}\)

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).

For every arm with \(\gamma_a<\infty\), \(F_a^{\pi}(t)=c_at^{\gamma_a-1}\{1+O(t^{\rho_a})\}\) as \(t\downarrow0\), with a remainder envelope, validity threshold, and positive parameter bounds common over the class.

novel.justification: This uniform second-order form strengthens the anchor's lawwise regular variation. Compact boundary-power charts with Hölder remainders satisfy it by uniform inversion.

standard.name: Finite inverse-propensity second moment for IPW scores

assumptions.condition: For every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\), fix the Borel regular conditional law \(t\mapsto K_a(t,\cdot)\) and, for every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the induced Borel regular conditional-score version \(\kappa_{a,\tau}(t)=\int\psi_{a,\tau}(y)K_a(t,dy)\); these chosen versions satisfy \(\sup_{a,\tau}|\kappa_{a,\tau}(t)-m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}|\le\omega_{\mathrm{mark}}(t)\) for all sufficiently small \(t>0\).

novel.justification: Fixing a common Borel conditional kernel makes every null-index endpoint evaluation and all nested scores jointly well posed, while the common score modulus holds in smooth conditional-location families with compactly bounded error scales.

assumptions.condition: \(\sup_{a,\tau,|v|\le u}|f_{a\mid X}(q_a(\tau)+v\mid X)-f_{a\mid X}(q_a(\tau)\mid X)|\to0\) almost surely as \(u\downarrow0\), under one deterministic modulus common over the class.

novel.justification: The common modulus is the uniform-curvature restriction absent from a lawwise density condition. Logistic location families with compact scale and location classes satisfy it.

This paper-specific coordinate restriction exposes boundary information explicitly. It is satisfied after a probability-integral-transform chart when the covariate index has a continuous distribution.

This chart includes polynomial approach to zero and smooth bounded-away arms under the explicit \(\gamma_a=\infty\) convention. Beta-like treatment rules and smooth multiplicative departures satisfy it.

assumptions.condition: Fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(t_\star>0\) satisfy \(\sup_{x:d_a(x)\le t_\star}\pi_a(x)\le1-\varepsilon\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\).

novel.justification: This local subclass restriction separates each studied zero-propensity endpoint from simultaneous near-deterministic assignment at that same endpoint. Two-sided logistic-odds charts satisfy it on fixed endpoint neighborhoods even when the opposite arm is heavy at the other endpoint.

assumptions.condition: Every \(g_a\) and \(m_{a,\tau}\) belongs to a fixed Hölder ball \(C^s([0,1])\) with \(s>1\).
Every arm satisfies \(\gamma_a\in[1+\epsilon_\gamma,2-\epsilon_\gamma]\cup[2+\epsilon_\gamma,\overline\gamma]\cup\{\infty\}\), for fixed \(\epsilon_\gamma>0\) and finite \(\overline\gamma\).

standard.name: Compact separation from a phase boundary

assumptions.condition: Every limiting scalar contrast used for coverage has a continuous distribution with a quantile modulus uniform over the class.

definitions.name: Boundary-adapted cross-fitted Bernoulli series learner
definitions.construction: For each arm and training sample excluding \(I_k\), maximize the Bernoulli likelihood over \(\log p_a(x)=\alpha\log d_a(x)+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_jB_{j,J_n}(x)\), with \(\alpha\ge0\) and \(p_a(x)\in(0,1)\), and select the unique deterministic-ridge-tie-broken maximizer. The same fit is used for every arm: a polynomial-tail arm has \(\alpha=\alpha_a>0\), while an arm bounded at the chart endpoint has \(\alpha=0\). The resulting function is \(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}\).
inputs: the prespecified arm chart and spline dictionary

definitions.name: Feasible positive-weight clipped-IPW quantile
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat t_{a,n}\) by the explicit generalized inverse, set \(\widehat h_{a,n}=1/\widehat t_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat b_{a,n}=\vartheta_a\widehat p_{a,(\lceil\widehat h_{a,n}\rceil\wedge n)}\), and define \(\widehat q_a(\tau)\) as the smallest minimizer of \(q\mapsto\sum_k\sum_{i\in I_k}\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}\rho_\tau(Y_i-q)/(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(X_i)\vee\widehat b_{a,n})\).

definitions.name: Centered local feasible objective
definitions.construction: \(\widehat Q_{a,n,\tau}(t)=nh_{a,n}^{-2}\sum_k\sum_{i\in I_k}\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(X_i)\vee\widehat b_{a,n})^{-1}[\rho_\tau\{Y_i-q_a(\tau)-th_{a,n}/n\}-\rho_\tau\{Y_i-q_a(\tau)\}]\). Population quantities only center and normalize this proof process.

definitions.name: Cross-fitted preliminary arm quantiles
definitions.construction: Within each outer training sample, use fixed inner folds to refit \(\text{def:boundary-learner}\), its generalized-inverse scale, and its order-statistic clipping threshold. Define \(\widetilde q_{a,-k}\) as the smallest inner-fold clipped-IPW minimizer and \(\widetilde\psi_{a,\tau,-k}(y)=\tau-\mathbf1\{y\le\widetilde q_{a,-k}(\tau)\}\).

definitions.name: Wholly empirical armwise clipping-drift correction
definitions.construction: For every arm, compute \(\widehat\gamma_a\) from the stated intermediate Hill formula and classify it by \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm H}\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm G}\). For an empirically heavy arm, compute \(\widehat m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}\), set \(\widehat\theta_a=\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\), and form \(\widehat\mu_{a,\theta}(\tau)=-\widehat\theta_a^{\widehat\gamma_a-1}\widehat m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}/\widehat\gamma_a\). For an empirically finite-variance arm, set \(\widehat\mu_{a,\theta}=0\). Compute \(\widehat f_a(\tau)\) from its displayed weighted kernel formula and set \(\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat q_a-(\widehat h_{a,n}/n)\widehat\mu_{a,\theta}/\widehat f_a\). All thresholds, scores, classifications, and densities are sample-computed; none uses \(q_a\), \(f_a\), \(m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}\), \(\theta_a\), \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\), or \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\).

definitions.name: Centered oracle Lévy score
definitions.construction: For \(t=(t_\tau)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\), define \[\log E\exp\{it^\top\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}\}=\int_0^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^R}\left[\exp\left\{i\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\frac{t_\tau u_\tau}{\max\{z,\theta_a\}}\right\}-1-i\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\frac{t_\tau u_\tau}{\max\{z,\theta_a\}}\right]H_a(du)(\gamma_a-1)z^{\gamma_a-1}dz.\] The Lévy integrand and \(\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}\) therefore depend on the endpoint input only through the declared score law \(H_a\).

definitions.name: Tail-band escape perturbation
definitions.construction: For \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\), multiply \(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)\) by \(1+M_n^{-(\gamma_a-1)}\) whenever \(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)\le M_n/\widehat h_{a,n}\), leave it unchanged elsewhere, and reapply the same probability-range constraint. Call the result \(\widehat\pi^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,-k}\), and compute \(E^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}\) and \(D^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}\) from that learner.

definitions.name: Refitted arm-vector \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) procedure
definitions.construction: Choose \(m\to\infty\) with \(m/n\to0\). Conditionally on the observed full sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), draw \(B\) according to \(\mathbb P_B\), uniformly over all subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) having cardinality \(m\). For every realized \(B\), refit all folds, generalized-inverse scales, order-statistic clips, preliminary quantiles, endpoint corrections, and densities. For \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), set \(V_{B,a}(\tau)=m\widehat H_{a,m,B}^{-1}\{\widehat q_{a,B}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)\}\), set \(T_{B,n}(\tau)=\widehat\ell_{1,n}V_{B,1}(\tau)-\widehat\ell_{0,n}V_{B,0}(\tau)\), and define \(c_{n,p}(\tau)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\mathbb P_B\{T_{B,n}(\tau)\le t\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}\ge p\}\). Thus the conditional law is the complete uniform empirical subsampling measure; conditionally independent draws from \(\mathbb P_B\) give its Monte Carlo approximation.
inputs: a conditional uniform randomizer over size-\(m\) subsets, or exact enumeration of all such subsets

definitions.name: Critical-resolution fold-experiment handle
definitions.construction: Represent training and evaluation extremes as one joint fold-labelled Poisson experiment, apply the measurable boundary-likelihood map induced by the constrained learner, and then map the weighted signed score through Knight's convex argmin identity.

statements.statement: The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) is nonempty in both mixed and two-heavy regimes. Set \(d_1(x)=x\) and \(d_0(x)=1-x\). A mixed neighborhood is generated by \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(\pi_1(x)=x^{3/2}/2\), \(\pi_0(x)=1-x^{3/2}/2\), and \(Y(a)=a+X+\zeta\) with centered logistic \(\zeta\): here \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}=\{1\}\), \(\gamma_1=5/3\), \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}=\{0\}\), and \(\gamma_0=\infty\) under the bounded-support convention. A two-heavy neighborhood is generated by \(\pi_1(x)=x^{\alpha_1}/\{x^{\alpha_1}+(1-x)^{\alpha_0}\}\) and \(\pi_0=1-\pi_1\), with compact \(\alpha_a>1\). Both neighborhoods obey common Hall, endpoint-score, and density moduli; the mixed center has nonzero treated endpoint drift at \(\tau=1/2\).
statements.justification: The explicit neighborhoods reconcile binary propensity coherence with either one or two weak-overlap endpoints.
statements.gap: The oracle anchor imposes lawwise tail behavior but does not construct a uniform smooth class for a growing propensity likelihood.
statements.consumer: These neighborhoods provide legal mixed-branch and two-heavy designs for the expansion and simulations.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\), heavy arms, fixed folds, and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the learner satisfies, up to a fixed power of \(\log n\), \[\sup_{d_a(x)\ge n^{-b_0}}|\log\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\log\pi_a(x)|=O_P(\delta_{a,n}),\] \[\left|\int m_{a,\tau}(x)\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}dP_X(x)\right|=O_P\left(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n\right),\] and the corresponding relative-error square integral is \(O_P(J_n^{-2s}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n)\). For \(J_n=\lfloor n^\xi\rfloor\) with \(1/\{s(\alpha_a+1)\}<\xi<1/(\alpha_a+1)\), there exists a deterministic \(M_n\uparrow\infty\) such that the sample-relevant punctured error obeys \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\), and \(\max_{\tau}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|=o_P(1)\). At \(\alpha_a=3/2\), \(s=3/2\), and \(J_n=\lfloor n^{0.3}\rfloor\), the displayed log-error is \(O_P(n^{-1/8}\operatorname{polylog}n)\) and the signed functional is \(O_P(n^{-17/40}\operatorname{polylog}n)\); hence any sufficiently slow \(M_n\) makes the amplified error vanish.
statements.justification: This is the early kill test and now derives, rather than assumes, the corrected amplified oracle-transfer condition.
statements.gap: Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder control a regular-overlap likelihood projection, not this singular signed Hall-boundary functional.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies a primitive flexible first stage for the non-Gaussian quantile argmin.

statements.statement: On the mixed center in \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), the control propensity satisfies \(\inf_x\pi_0(x)=1/2\), \(t_{0,n}\to1/2\), \(h_{0,n}\to2\), \(\widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P1/2\), and \(\widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\vartheta_0/2<1/2\). Thus clipping is asymptotically inactive on the control arm, its drift correction is exactly zero by construction, and its feasible objective equals the untrimmed fitted-weight objective with probability tending to one.
statements.justification: This recomputation removes the nonvanishing-clipping error created by allowing multipliers above one.
statements.gap: This is a required sanity reduction, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It verifies that the feasible rule targets the untrimmed control quantile on the explicit mixed-regime witness.

statements.statement: Write \(R=|\mathcal T|\) and order the finite index set as \(\tau_{(1)}<\cdots<\tau_{(R)}\). The threshold indicators \(\mathbf1\{Y(a)\le q_a(\tau_{(r)})\}\) are nested, so \(\Psi_a(Y(a))\) is supported on the \(R+1\) cells cut out by the ordered thresholds. For every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\) and every sufficiently small \(t>0\), \[\left\|K_a(t,\cdot)\circ\Psi_a^{-1}-H_a\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\left\|\operatorname{Law}\{\Psi_a(Y(a))\mid\pi_a(X)=t\}-H_a\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le R\,\omega_{\mathrm{mark}}(t).\] Indeed, each endpoint cell probability differs by at most \(\omega_{\mathrm{mark}}(t)\) and each interior cell probability is a difference of two adjacent threshold probabilities. Moreover, if \(\widetilde G_a((-\infty,q_a(\tau)])=G_a((-\infty,q_a(\tau)])\) for every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), then \(\widetilde G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}=H_a\); hence the law in \(\text{def:oracle-limit}\) is invariant to replacing \(G_a\) by \(\widetilde G_a\).
statements.justification: The finite collection of quantile scores records only nested threshold-cell probabilities, so coordinate score moduli control the entire endpoint mark vector in total variation.
statements.gap: The oracle anchor is written with an endpoint outcome-mark law; this lemma isolates the strictly smaller score-law object actually used by its finite-quantile Lévy integrand.
statements.consumer: The feasible oracle-transfer theorem can invoke a common score modulus without assuming convergence of the full conditional outcome law at the propensity endpoint.

statements.statement: For every heavy arm, choose \(J_n\) and the derived \(M_n\) from \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\). Then the deterministic and centered Knight remainders of \(\widehat Q_{a,n,\tau}\) converge uniformly on compact local-parameter sets to \(f_a(\tau)t^2/2\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\theta_a=\vartheta_a\), the preliminary quantiles and every wholly empirical drift component are consistent, and \[\left(\frac{n}{h_{a,n}}\{\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)}{f_a(\tau)}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}.\] By \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\), the endpoint mark step requires only total-variation convergence of the finite score vector \(\Psi_a(Y(a))\) to \(H_a\); no convergence of the full conditional outcome law is required. The true-propensity fixed-quantile law is recovered by replacing the fitted propensity and empirical clip by their population counterparts.
statements.justification: It converts the oracle heavy-tail benchmark into a feasible growing-sieve theorem, with its transfer condition proved from primitives.
statements.gap: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky prove the observed-true-propensity fixed-quantile law and no feasible propensity-estimation theorem.
statements.consumer: Observational QTE analyses can use flexible assignment models while retaining full-population non-Gaussian calibration.

statements.statement: The amplification order is intrinsic. On the nonzero-drift mixed witness, the escape learner satisfies \(E^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}\to_P1\) and \(D^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}\to_P0\), preserves every fixed-window endpoint mark limit, but shifts the normalized feasible heavy-arm quantile by \(-m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}/f_a(\tau)\). Therefore uniform oracle transfer for this perturbed sequence requires vanishing control at the order \(E^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}\); the order is not a sufficient-rate artifact.
statements.justification: The separately notated perturbation isolates compensator mass that fixed-window convergence misses.
statements.gap: No located QTE result gives an escaping-tail-band necessity theorem for learned inverse weights.
statements.consumer: The result gives a sharp diagnostic for whether a boundary learner can inherit oracle calibration.

statements.statement: For every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\), the data-driven clip is asymptotically inactive when the propensity is bounded away from zero and is first-order negligible otherwise under \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\). The cross-fitted likelihood construction satisfies \[\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{IF}_a(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1)\] jointly over \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), with covariance \(E_P[\mathrm{IF}_a\mathrm{IF}_{a'}^\top]\).
statements.justification: The Gaussian branch retains shared first-stage covariance and is now centered at the correct untrimmed quantile.
statements.gap: Firpo establishes the regular-overlap result; the present branch allows finite inverse moments without strict overlap and is supporting machinery for mixed regimes.
statements.consumer: It supplies the regular component of a QTE whose other arm can have an infinitely divisible limit.

statements.statement: Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\), along each subsequence with \(\ell_{a,n}\to\ell_a\), \[\frac{n}{H_n}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta)\Rightarrow\ell_1L_1-\ell_0L_0,\] where \(L_a=\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}/f_a\) for \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\) and \(L_a\) is the Gaussian vector generated by \(\mathrm{IF}_a\) for \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\). Unequal heavy indices are dominated by the smaller index, equal heavy indices retain both endpoint constants, a heavy arm dominates a finite-variance arm, and two finite-variance arms retain their shared learned-score covariance. The two oracle-preserved heavy-arm endpoint processes are independent because their rare-event endpoint sets are disjoint.
statements.justification: The explicit arm partition makes equal, unequal, and mixed regimes coherent without inventing a Hall index for a bounded arm.
statements.gap: The oracle QTE paper gives joint endpoint laws but not recombination with a shared flexible propensity likelihood.
statements.consumer: Analysts obtain joint QTE inference when treatment and control have different overlap regimes.

statements.statement: Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\) and \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), conditionally on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the law of the vector \((T_{B,n}(\tau))_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\) consistently estimates the limit in \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\). For every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the pointwise interval \[\left[\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}c_{n,1-\alpha/2}(\tau),\;\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\frac{\widehat H_n}{n}c_{n,\alpha/2}(\tau)\right]\] has asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\). For local unequal-heavy-tail sequences whose index gap has exact order \(1/\log n\), raw scalar QTE subsampling at any fixed polynomial rate strictly between constant and linear generally converges to the wrong arm mixture.
statements.justification: Armwise refitting reproduces first-stage uncertainty and repairs the near-equal-index scalar-mixture failure.
statements.gap: Heiler and Kazak treat scalar mean-type irregular statistics, not two learned convex argmins with unequal arm scales.
statements.consumer: The theorem yields the displayed implementable pointwise confidence interval for each reported quantile across heavy, mixed, and Gaussian QTE regimes.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{fold}}\), characterize the joint limit of learned endpoint marks, their compensator, and the feasible convex argmin when \(nJ_n^{-(\alpha_a+1)}\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\). Determine necessary and sufficient primitive conditions for an infinitely divisible limit, a Cox mixture, or a more general fold-coupled Poisson functional.
statements.justification: Order-one training-fold boundary information can couple evaluation marks despite cross-fitting.
statements.gap: The located work has oracle weights, regular likelihood scores, or scalar stable sums, not a fold-labelled critical boundary experiment.
statements.consumer: A solution would support aggressive propensity adaptation outside the subcritical preservation window.

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under conditional unconfoundedness; identification is given and the contribution is limit theory.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with a declared partition into Hall-heavy arms and finite-inverse-moment arms.
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity almost surely; each heavy arm has a uniform second-order Hall lower tail, while each Gaussian arm has a uniformly finite inverse propensity moment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold constrained Bernoulli series likelihood; all scales use an explicit generalized inverse, clipping uses fitted-propensity order statistics with multipliers strictly below one, endpoint scores use nested cross-fitted preliminary quantiles, and the full algorithm is refitted inside each conditionally uniform size-\(m\) subsample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 combines Proposition 8.2's deterministic quadratic Knight-remainder and process limit with Proposition 8.3's finite-dimensional infinitely divisible Lévy score limit for the observed true-propensity clipped fixed-quantile estimator.
A growing series-logit propensity fit yields efficient regular-overlap IPW mean estimation.
A nonparametric estimated-propensity QTE estimator is root-\(n\) normal and efficient under regular overlap.
Adaptive scalar \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) resampling yields inference for mean-type effects under irregular identification.
Thresholded cross-fitted AIPW means admit Gaussian inference under tail-amplified nuisance conditions.
Balance-fitted propensities yield regular limit theory for distributional and quantile treatment effects.

tldr: A boundary-adapted growing Bernoulli likelihood can preserve the infinitely divisible clipped-IPW quantile law under Hall weak overlap. For the finite target set, the endpoint law enters only through the pushforward \(H_a=G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}\), and the primitive coordinate score modulus yields total-variation convergence of that finite score law without full endpoint outcome-law convergence. The signed-functional expansion derives \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\) for the displayed learner, while a separately defined escape learner proves the amplification order is intrinsically necessary. The fully sample-driven procedure supports heavy, Gaussian, joint unequal-tail, and conditionally uniform refitted arm-vector subsampling with explicit pointwise confidence intervals; the critical fold-labelled Poisson law remains open.

project_justification.gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE theorem uses the observed true propensity. Regular estimated-propensity quantile and series-logit results rely on regular overlap, and weak-overlap nuisance results concern smooth means rather than a moving quantile boundary.
project_justification.niche: A feasible full-population QTE estimator needs a signed likelihood expansion that respects Hall endpoint geometry, convex check loss, clipping drift, and shared folds.
project_justification.fill: The project factors the endpoint Lévy law through the finite score pushforward, derives its total-variation convergence from the primitive coordinate score modulus, derives the amplified transfer condition from a boundary likelihood fit, proves its intrinsic order through an escape perturbation, separates heavy and finite-variance arms, gives a wholly empirical correction, and validates conditionally uniform arm-vector subsampling with explicit pointwise confidence intervals.

related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky (2025, arXiv:2506.18215v1) provide the observed true-propensity fixed-quantile result in Theorem 3.1: Proposition 8.2 gives the deterministic quadratic Knight-remainder and process limit, and Proposition 8.3 gives the finite-dimensional infinitely divisible Lévy score limit. On the finite target set used here, that Lévy integrand factors through \(H_a=G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}\), so the needed endpoint convergence concerns only nested quantile scores rather than the full conditional outcome law; the paper supplies no feasible propensity-estimation theorem. Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003) inform the growing-likelihood projection under strict overlap. Firpo (2007) informs the regular quantile influence function under strict overlap. Ma and Wang (2020) inform heavy-tail centering for linear IPW means. Heiler and Kazak (2021) inform scalar irregular subsampling. Dorn (2025) informs tail-amplified cross-fit remainder accounting for orthogonal means. Sant'Anna, Song, and Xu (2022) inform regular balance-fitted distributional estimation. None of these informed-by comparisons is presented as a strict theorem extension.
technical_internal_limitation: Hall tails alone do not imply uniform propensity learnability, so uniform claims use the boundary-smooth subclass and the proposal proves explicit mixed and two-heavy member neighborhoods. Exactly the finite-variance boundary is excluded. The endpoint restriction controls only the finite nested score vector and does not assert convergence of the full conditional outcome law. The infinitely divisible learned-mark description is not asserted for arbitrary critical-resolution shared-fold learners.
honest_scope: The anchor's oracle convex limit is Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2506.18215v1, with the deterministic process step in Proposition 8.2 and the finite-dimensional Lévy score step in Proposition 8.3. Its finite-quantile Lévy integrand depends on \(G_a\) only through \(H_a=G_a\circ\Psi_a^{-1}\); the derived nested-cell lemma must prove that the primitive score modulus implies total-variation convergence to \(H_a\), and no full endpoint outcome-law convergence is assumed. The boundary likelihood expansion, scale consistency, preliminary-score correction, intrinsic transfer necessity, Gaussian projection, arm recombination, and conditionally uniform refitted pointwise inference remain to be proved. The critical fold law is open. The finite-variance sanity reduction is explicit: on the mixed center, \(h_{0,n}\to2\) and \(\widehat b_{0,n}\to\vartheta_0/2<1/2=\inf_x\pi_0(x)\), so the control clip disappears and the estimator centers at \(q_0\).
